title: Katharine Drexel (1858–1955)
hookLine: an heiress who gave her fortune to schools for Black and Native Americans

cards: Rome, and a young woman from a banking family in Philadelphia kneels before Pope Leo XIII. She has come to ask a favor.
Back home she has seen missions among Native American peoples that are short of priests, and she wants the Pope to send missionaries.
Tradition says he answered with a question of his own: why not become a missionary yourself? It was not the answer she came for. It changed the plan.

teach.b: Start with the money. First, the inheritance. Her father, Francis Drexel, was a wealthy banker, and when he died, the income from his fortune passed to his daughters.
Katharine's share was large. Second, the vow.

teach.h: THE SISTERS OF THE BLESSED SACRAMENT.
teach.b: Instead of marrying or living quietly on the money, she became a sister and founded a new community, the Sisters of the Blessed Sacrament.
Their work was with Native Americans and Black Americans, among them children whom segregated schools often turned away. Third, the giving.

teach.h: SCHOOLS PAID FOR, YEAR AFTER YEAR.
teach.b: Year after year she paid for schools, missions and churches, in the West and the South, in cities and on reservations. In New Orleans she and her sisters founded what became Xavier University of Louisiana.
People wrote asking for help, and she answered letter after letter. Her biographers say she lived plainly herself: worn shoes, patched clothes, pencils used down to the stub. Fourth, the quiet end.

teach.h: A QUIET ROOM BY THE CHAPEL.
teach.b: After illness she spent her last years mostly in prayer, in a small room near the chapel, close to the Blessed Sacrament she had named her sisters for.
In Matthew's Gospel, a rich young man asks Jesus what he must do, and Jesus tells him to sell what he has, give to the poor, and follow. The young man walks away sad, because he has many possessions.
Katharine Drexel heard the same Gospel and did not walk away. The Church has since canonized her.

how: Catholics in the United States keep Katharine Drexel's feast in March; the Sisters of the Blessed Sacrament, Xavier University of Louisiana and Black and Native American Catholic communities mark it with Mass and service.

games.q: you're a rich young woman asking the Pope for missionaries. he asks why you don't become one yourself. what do you do?
o: send a large check and go home.
become a sister and spend your inheritance on schools.
find a priest to go in your place.
games.why: she became a sister, founded a community, and gave the fortune to schools and missions.

practice: Let a child or a student come to mind whose chance to learn is fragile, and a place that helps them: a school near you, a scholarship fund, a library, a tutoring program.
Ask what one gift could look like there, money or time or a box of books. If you pray, pray for the students by name or by face; if not, simply stay with them a while.
